set -eu

# @tbhb runs this script once, in their own terminal, and 1Password asks
# them to approve once.
# An agent only prints it. It needs op, jq and security.
# It first creates each vault it needs that the account lacks.
# It grants the Connect server srv its vaults, then creates one token with no expiry for each host
# and stores it in the host's vault as the item connect-token, field token.
# A host whose vault already holds connect-token is skipped, so the script is safe
# to run again.
# ex-ctl1 also gets an ops-session token, which reads every
# agent host's vault, writes host-0-shared and reads the vault overlay-oauth,
# which holds the Tailscale OAuth client that mints runner-VM auth keys.
# It goes into the keychain of the user who runs the script, with no
# ssh, and into no vault. It is skipped if that keychain already holds
# it.

vaults=$(op vault list --account acct.example.com --format json) || {
  echo 'could not list the vaults in the 1Password account' >&2
  exit 1
}
for name in host-0-shared host-ex-ctl1 host-ex-ctl2 host-ex-lab1 host-ex-win1 overlay-oauth; do
  found=$(printf '%s' "$vaults" | jq -r --arg name "$name" 'any(.[]; .name == $name)') || {
    echo 'could not read the vault list' >&2
    exit 1
  }
  if [ "$found" = false ]; then
    op vault create --account acct.example.com "$name" >/dev/null
    echo "created vault $name"
  fi
done
unset vaults

op connect vault grant --account acct.example.com --server srv --vault host-0-shared
op connect vault grant --account acct.example.com --server srv --vault host-ex-ctl1
op connect vault grant --account acct.example.com --server srv --vault host-ex-ctl2
op connect vault grant --account acct.example.com --server srv --vault host-ex-lab1
op connect vault grant --account acct.example.com --server srv --vault host-ex-win1
op connect vault grant --account acct.example.com --server srv --vault overlay-oauth

# ex-lab1
if op item get --account acct.example.com connect-token --vault host-ex-lab1 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo 'host-ex-lab1 already holds connect-token; skipping' >&2
else
  tok=$(op connect token create --account acct.example.com 'agent-host:ex-lab1:20261108T142100Z' --server srv --vault host-ex-lab1,r --vault host-0-shared,r)
  if [ -z "$tok" ]; then
    echo 'op connect token create printed no token for ex-lab1' >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  printf '%s' "$tok" \
    | jq -R '{title: "connect-token", category: "API_CREDENTIAL", fields: [{label: "token", type: "CONCEALED", value: .}]}' \
    | op item create --account acct.example.com --vault host-ex-lab1 -
  unset tok
fi

# ops-session ex-ctl1
if ! sh -c 'mkdir -p ~/Library/Keychains && { [ -e ~/Library/Keychains/ops-connect.keychain-db ] || security create-keychain -p "" ops-connect.keychain; } && security unlock-keychain -p "" ops-connect.keychain && security set-keychain-settings ops-connect.keychain'; then
  echo 'could not prepare your keychain on ex-ctl1' >&2
  exit 1
fi
rc=0
security find-generic-password -s ops-connect -a agent ops-connect.keychain >/dev/null 2>&1 || rc=$?
case $rc in
  0)
    echo 'your keychain on ex-ctl1 already holds ops-connect; skipping' >&2
    ;;
  44)
    tok=$(op connect token create --account acct.example.com 'ops-session:ex-ctl1:20261108T142100Z' --server srv --vault host-0-shared --vault host-ex-ctl1,r --vault host-ex-ctl2,r --vault host-ex-lab1,r --vault host-ex-win1,r --vault overlay-oauth,r)
    if [ -z "$tok" ]; then
      echo 'op connect token create printed no token for ops-session ex-ctl1' >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    case $tok in
      *[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*)
        echo 'the ops-session token for ex-ctl1 has a character the keychain line cannot carry' >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
    esac
    stored=false
    if [ "${#tok}" -gt 4002 ]; then
      echo "the ops-session token for ex-ctl1 has ${#tok} characters, over the 4002 the keychain line can carry" >&2
    elif echo "add-generic-password -U -s ops-connect -a agent -T /usr/bin/security -w $tok ops-connect.keychain" | { security unlock-keychain -p "" ops-connect.keychain && security -i; } >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      stored=true
    else
      echo 'the ops-session token for ex-ctl1 was made but not stored' >&2
    fi
    if [ "$stored" = false ]; then
      if op connect token delete --account acct.example.com 'ops-session:ex-ctl1:20261108T142100Z' --server srv >/dev/null; then
        echo 'deleted the ops-session token ops-session:ex-ctl1:20261108T142100Z from srv' >&2
      else
        echo 'could not delete the ops-session token ops-session:ex-ctl1:20261108T142100Z; delete it by hand with op connect token delete' >&2
      fi
      exit 1
    fi
    unset tok
    if ! security find-generic-password -s ops-connect -a agent ops-connect.keychain >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo 'your keychain on ex-ctl1 does not hold the token' >&2
      exit 1
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    echo 'could not look in your keychain on ex-ctl1' >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac
